H04.description: remove_colliding deletes any agent-added .py whose bare basename matches a hidden/fixture test-dir .py (including helpers and modules inside packages, e.g. src/pkg/helpers.py), so correct solutions lose files and fail, while it misses real pytest import-name collisions in packages, ignores files inside directory overlays and the task's python_files setting.

H07.description: The auth.json copy placed in the agent-readable per-run HOME keeps a long-lived OPENAI_API_KEY verbatim, exposing the operator's API key to the agent under evaluation.
H07.reason: severity: codebook critical (a credential exposed verbatim); agreed otherwise

H12.description: Adds variables for the horizon override and the in-memory pre-flight record used by the horizon fix.
H12.reason: follow-on of the horizon fix D3 (A's namespace): the override knob and the record variable belong to that fix

H13.description: Validates the new horizon override knob.

H14.description: On --resume the codex pre-flight counts every plan entry (including already-rowed trials) toward the token horizon, so a resume whose remaining trials fit the token's lifetime is wrongly refused.
H14.reason: verdict: counting already-rowed trials on --resume is a wrong behaviour of its own, distinct from the horizon formula (D3) — defect (A), own group D4

H15.description: Adds auth_mode/trials_counted/horizon_source fields and a note slot to the pre-flight record for the fixed check.
H15.reason: follow-on of D3 in both (membership differs only through H14)

H16.description: The required horizon 2 x sum(watchdog)/concurrency can be shorter than a single trial's own watchdog, so a token that expires mid-trial passes the pre-flight (and an API-key-mode auth.json without tokens.access_token is wrongly refused).
H16.reason: severity: codebook high — a failure on a common path (every batch runs concurrency > 1)

H17.description: Updates the refusal message for the new horizon formula, prints the API-key note and keeps the record in a variable instead of a scratch file.

H18.description: write_manifest reads the pre-flight record from the variable rather than the scratch file.
H18.reason: class: follow-on — the caller reads the record from the variable the D3 fix introduced (H17); refactor rejected

H20.description: Passes the pre-flight record to write_status so STATUS.json can carry this invocation's record (trials counted on resume).
H20.reason: follow-on: pre-flight record plumbing belongs to D3 with H17–H19
